coffee.name: Knots Coffee Roasters
coffee.location: Queen Kapiolani Hotel, 150 Kapahulu Ave -- across from the Honolulu Zoo, ~10 min walk from central Waikiki
coffee.why: Roasts in-house and sources from Big Island Coffee Roasters and Maui Coffee Roasters with actual origin info on the bag, not just a 'Kona blend' sticker. Open-air patio right on the path to the Zoo and beach -- closest thing to a Heart/Prince-style roastery you'll find in Waikiki proper.

coffee.name: Morning Glass Coffee
coffee.location: 2955 E Manoa Rd, Manoa -- 15-20 min drive/rideshare from Waikiki
coffee.why: Worth the trip out of the tourist core: house-roasted, genuinely excellent espresso in a tucked-away residential neighborhood where actual locals hang out. Pair it with their breakfast menu (mac+cheese pancakes, breakfast burrito) and make it a whole outing rather than a coffee run.

food.name: Da Cove Health Bar
food.location: Near Kaimana Beach, base of Diamond Head -- ~20 min walk down the beach from central Waikiki
food.why: The local consensus pick for acai bowls on Oahu -- small, always-busy spot with fresh fruit smoothies and wild-caught ahi wraps. Great pre- or post- Diamond Head stop, and a much better quick option than the smoothie stands lining Kalakaua.

food.name: Hau Tree
food.location: Kaimana Beach Hotel, 2863 Kalakaua Ave -- oceanfront, edge of Waikiki toward Diamond Head
food.why: Tables right in the sand under a century-old hau tree with Diamond Head in view -- about as good as a breakfast setting gets here. Crab eggs benedict is the move. It's pricier and the food plays second fiddle to the setting, so treat this as the sit-down option when you've actually got time, not an everyday spot.

food.name: Honolulu Burger Company
food.location: 2919 Kapiolani Blvd, Kaimuki -- ~10 min drive from Waikiki
food.why: Grass-fed beef from family-owned Hawaii ranches, hand-cut fries, real milkshakes -- a legitimately good burger from a local company, not a tourist-trap burger shack. Worth the short drive when you want a burger that's actually worth it.

bars.name: Green Lady Cocktail Room
bars.location: White Sands Hotel, 431 Nohonani St, Waikiki
bars.why: Unmarked door flush with the bamboo wall left of the hotel entrance -- ask for 'Room 8.' Walk-ins only, open 8pm-1am, classic speakeasy vibe with creative cocktails ($16-20). The kind of place you'd only find if someone told you about it.

bars.name: SKY Waikiki -- BACKBAR
bars.location: SKY Waikiki, 2270 Kalakaua Ave, rooftop level
bars.why: A hidden bar behind a wall inside SKY Waikiki's rooftop space -- started as an invite-only secret, now open Tue-Sun from 5pm. Good second stop after dinner if Green Lady's packed.

activities.name: Diamond Head Summit Trail (sunrise)
activities.location: Diamond Head State Monument -- ~10 min drive or scenic walk from Waikiki via Kapiolani Park
activities.why: 20-30 min hike up a WWII-era crater to a 360-degree view of Waikiki and the south shore -- best before the heat and crowds. Reservations open 30 days out on recreation.gov and sunrise slots (6-7am) sell out within hours, so book this as soon as the trip is confirmed.
activities.book_ahead: Reserve on recreation.gov starting 30 days before the visit date -- sunrise slots (6-7am) sell out within hours of opening.

activities.name: Airbnb Experience -- Haku Lei Making
activities.location: Hosted locally, varies by host -- typically Waikiki/Honolulu area
activities.why: Small-group lesson on making a traditional Hawaiian flower crown with a local host, plus the cultural history behind it -- a genuine 'local friend teaches you something' experience instead of the souvenir-shop version.

activities.name: Kaka'ako Art District
activities.location: Kaka'ako neighborhood -- ~10 min drive from Waikiki
activities.why: Block after block of large-scale murals from the POW WOW Hawaii festival, plus indie galleries and coffee shops -- a completely different, art-school side of Honolulu that most Waikiki visitors never see.

free.name: Kuhio Beach Hula Show
free.location: Kuhio Beach, near the Duke Kahanamoku statue, Waikiki
free.why: Free Hawaiian music and hula under the stars, Tue/Thu/Sat evenings -- low-key, local-run, and right on the beach. Worth checking which of those days falls in the trip window.

free.name: Hilton Hawaiian Village Friday Fireworks
free.why: Every Friday at 7:45pm, free to watch from the beach or lagoon area -- good excuse for an evening beach walk regardless of where you're staying.

free.name: Sans Souci / Kaimana Beach sunset
free.location: Sans Souci Beach Park, edge of Waikiki toward Diamond Head
free.why: Quieter than the main Waikiki strip, popular with local families for evening swims and picnics, and a great low-key sunset spot with Diamond Head as the backdrop.
